questions.question: Two circles touch each other internally. Their radii are 3 cm and 4 cm. What is the length of the biggest chord of the circle with radii 4 cm which is outside the inner circle?
questions.solution:
Given:

Two circles touch each other internally.

The radius of the inner circle = 3 cm

The radius of the outer circle = 4 cm

**Concept used:**

When two circles are touch each other internally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a92ef9f5aaba595f851324c4c2d592b700849ddb68fcebcdbf27bbff1cd82e8.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cf8598b36fb0aa6b3f3cd504c8f27f3bce39a376be2c6c56d7e97dfd761c0c1.png] 

When the largest chord of bigger circle is tangent to the inner circle (smaller circle).

Then, 

Radius of inner circle (PD) = x cm

Radius of bigger circle (OB) = y cm

OP = Distance between two centers = Radius of bigger circle - radius of inner circle

⇒OP = y - x

CD = Diameter of inner circle = 2 × (radius of inner circle)

⇒ CD = 2x

OC = Difference between chord and bigger circle centre = CD - PD - OP

OC = CD - PD - OP

⇒ OC = 2x - x - (y - x) = 2x - y

Calculation:

Let the biggest chord of the circle with radii 4 cm which is outside the inner circle = AB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a92ef9f5aaba595f851324c4c2d592b700849ddb68fcebcdbf27bbff1cd82e8.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cf8598b36fb0aa6b3f3cd504c8f27f3bce39a376be2c6c56d7e97dfd761c0c1.png] 

From the figure, we know that

PD = 3 cm 

OD = 4 cm

OP = OD - PD

⇒ OP = 4 - 3 = 1 cm

⇒ CD = 2 x PD = 2 x 3 = 6 cm

OC = CD - PD - OP

⇒ OC = 6 - 3 - 1 = 2 cm

⇒ OB = 4 cm = radius of outer circle

By using Pythagoras theorem, we can write that

OB2 = BC2 + OC2

⇒ 42 = BC2 + 22

⇒ BC2 = 16 - 4

⇒ BC2 = 12

⇒ BC = sqrt{12} = 2sqrt{3} cm

Now, 

The length of biggest chord AB = 2 x BC = 2 x 2sqrt{3} = 4sqrt{3} cm

**∴ The length of the biggest chord of the circle outside the inner circle is 4sqrt{3} cm.**

questions.question: A circle is with center O. Two tangents AP and AQ are drawn from an external point A. If ∠POQ is equal to 118°. Then find the ∠PAQ:
questions.solution:
**Given :-**

A circle is with center O

Two tangents AP and AQ are drawn from an external point A.

∠POQ = 118°

**Concept :- **

Length of tangents drawn from an outside point to a circle are equal. 

It also makes an quadrilateral. 

In a quadrilateral sum of all angles are 360° 

**Calculation :-**

⇒ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18b1f2b54b4c9271ed113f091bd58a6a52b7cb10150df95d6c59a7ee1cdfa7eb.png] 

⇒ As OP and OQ is radius 

⇒ OP = OQ 

⇒ PA = PQ (From circle properties)

⇒ ∠APO = ∠AQO = 90° (As OP and OQ is perpendicular to PA and AQ)

⇒ Sum of angles = ∠P + ∠O + ∠Q + ∠A 

⇒ 360° = 90° + 118° + 90° + ∠A

⇒ 360° - (90° + 118° + 90°) = ∠A

⇒ 360° - 298° = ∠A

⇒ ∠A = 62° 

⇒ The ∠PAQ = 62° 

**∴ ∠PAQ = 62° **

r₁ and r₂ = radius of the circles

⇒ Length of the tangent = sqrt{324 - 196} = sqrt{128}

⇒ Length of the tangent = 8sqrt{2} cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8sqrt{2} cm. Option 3).**

questions.question: Consider AD is a tangent to a circle of radius 6 cm. AC is a secant meeting the circle at B and CD is a diameter. If AB is 7 cm, then the value of AC (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 6 cm

AB = 7 cm

CD = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

**Formula used:**

AD² = AC × AB

AC² - CD² = AD²

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b186b8aac889f8998a954c1157c7da19637a4433557a57e81575aa4777b0ba34.png] 

Substituting the values in the Tangent-Secant Theorem:

AC² - 12² = AC × 7

⇒ AC² - 144 = 7AC

⇒ AC² - 7AC - 144 = 0

This is a quadratic equation, solving using the quadratic formula:

⇒ AC2 - 16AC + 9AC - 144 = 0

⇒ AC(AC - 16) + 9(AC - 16) = 0

⇒ (AC - 16)(AC + 9) = 0

⇒ AC = 16 or AC = -9

⇒ AC = 16 cm (since length cannot be negative)

**∴ The value of AC is 16 cm.**

questions.question: The tangent at a point A of a circle with centre O intersects the diameter PQ of the circle (when extended) at the point B. If ∠BAP = 125°, then ∠AQP is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A circle with center O and diameter PQ extended outside the circle to point B

∠BAP = 125°

**Concept Used:**

Angle formed between radius and tangent of a circle is always 90°

Angles opposite to equal sides are equal.

Sum of two opposite interior angles of a triangle is equal to the opposite exterior angle.

Sum of all angles of triangle is 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/448c1a81df5301d2c8370fb3ff5373bb257ef0afaad4d494b08f4d9816fe1762.png] 

OA ⊥ BA (Angle between Radius and Tangent)

∠OAP = ∠BAP - ∠OAB

⇒ ∠OAP = 125° - 90° = 35°

Since,

OA = OP = OQ (Radius of circle)

So,

∠OAP = ∠OPA = 35°

∠AOQ = ∠OAP + ∠OPA

⇒ ∠AOQ = 35° + 35° = 70°

In Δ AOQ,

∠AOQ = 70°

∠OAQ = ∠OQA (since OA = OQ)

∠AOQ + ∠OAQ + ∠OQA = 180°

⇒ 70° + ∠OAQ + ∠OQA = 180°

⇒ ∠OAQ + ∠OQA = 180° - 70° = 110°

⇒ 2∠OQA = 110°/2 = 55°

Since ∠OQA is the same angle as ∠AQP

∠AQP = 55°

**∴**** The value of ****∠****AQP = 55° **

**Calculations:**

Let us draw two circles with centre O and centre M and radius 4 cm and 6 cm respectively.

Rightarrow Angle AOC = Angle BMC ( OA and MB are perpendicular to the same line AB. So, OA || MB, Thus, by alternate angle theorem Angle AOC = Angle BMC)

Hence, ∆AOC ≈ ∆BMC

therefore, (AO)/(BM)=(OC)/(MC)= (4)/(6) =(2)/(3)

**Hence, The Required ratio is 2 : 3.**

questions.question: The sides AB, BC and AC of ΔABC are 12 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, respectively. A circle is inscribed in the triangle touching AB, BC and AC at D, E and F, respectively. The ratio of the lengths of AD to CE is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sides AB, BC and AC of ΔABC are 12 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm.

A circle is inscribed in the triangle touching AB, BC and AC at D, E and F.

**Concept Used:**

Length of tangents from a fixed point outside the circle is always same.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/573f6cebf0f4bfe3d26b584956f449cd063109283a9bc2bad77959482a5abf93.png] 

Let length of AD = AF = x

Length of BD = BE = y

And length of CE = CF = z

Now,

2 × (x + y + z) = (12 + 8 + 10)

⇒ x + y + z = 15

Again,

AB = (x + y) = 12 cm

BC = (y + z) = 8 cm

CA = (x + z) = 10 cm

Now, x = (x + y + z) – (y + z) = 15 – 8 = 7 cm

z = (x + y + z) – (x + y) = 15 – 12 = 3 cm

AD : CE = 7 : 3

**∴ Ratio of the lengths of AD to CE is 7 : 3**
